market_context: United States; trans-fat regulation and labeling
title: What Does “Partially Hydrogenated Oil” Mean, and Why Does It Matter?

seo.title: Partially Hydrogenated Oil: What It Means
seo.meta_description: Partial hydrogenation makes liquid oil more solid but can create trans fat. FDA removed partially hydrogenated oils from generally recognized as safe status.
seo.search_intent: Explain partial hydrogenation and why the ingredient became a major trans-fat concern.

excerpt: Partially hydrogenated oil is liquid oil that has had hydrogen added to some of its double bonds to make it firmer and more stable. The process can create industrial trans fat, which is why partially hydrogenated oils were removed from routine approved food use in the United States.
content_html:
“Hydrogenated” describes a chemical change, not a mysterious source ingredient. Partial hydrogenation saturates some double bonds in an oil while allowing others to shift into the trans configuration.

Why manufacturers used it

Turning part of a liquid oil into firmer fat improved texture, oxidative stability, and shelf life in products such as shortening, frosting, and older margarines. The trade-off was the creation of industrial trans fatty acids.

Why trans fat became a public-health target

Trans fat raises LDL cholesterol and is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. FDA determined that partially hydrogenated oils were no longer generally recognized as safe, leading to their removal from ordinary U.S. food formulations.

Partially and fully hydrogenated are different

Fully hydrogenating an oil saturates far more double bonds and can leave little trans fat, although the resulting fat may be high in saturated fat. “Partially hydrogenated” is the phrase historically tied most directly to industrial trans-fat exposure.

faq.question: Is partially hydrogenated oil the same as trans fat?
faq.answer: Not exactly, but partial hydrogenation creates trans fatty acids and was historically a major industrial source.

faq.question: Does fully hydrogenated oil contain trans fat?
faq.answer: It generally contains far less trans fat than partially hydrogenated oil, but it can be high in saturated fat.

faq.question: Is partially hydrogenated oil still allowed in U.S. foods?
faq.answer: FDA removed partially hydrogenated oils from generally recognized as safe status, so they are no longer used as a routine approved ingredient.
